description: §19.16.6 (S430 round 6, B) — a block that contains a `defer` and declares `function g` twice is E-DEFER-DUPLICATE-FUNCTION (exactly once, naming both declarations) instead of an E-CODEGEN-INVALID-LOGIC crash. The same function WITHOUT the defer compiles (duplicate-function-no-defer-ok) — this is one of the listed fail-closed exceptions to 'a defer does not change what compiles'.
rationale: §19.16.6: the lowered block is a host try block, where a second declaration of the same function name is not allowed; the compiler SHALL name both declarations rather than fail at codegen. §7.3.3 (duplicate functions outside this case) is unchanged.
